meta.method_misses: Top-level method_misses lists each design decision the founder raised that the ledger held no row for: date (YYYY-MM-DD), lead (his words), family (a meta.sources family that should have caught it) and issue (the issue that re-checks that family). Procedure: docs/coverage-ledger-method.md §8 (#267).
meta.jobs_done: A job marked done gives done (the issue that filled it, as #275) and destinations (where each research line its rows cite went). The forms, and what node ledger-upkeep.js --check refuses: docs/coverage-ledger-method.md §6 (#266).
meta.method: docs/coverage-ledger-method.md, by #210: blind coders extracted one row per decision (property x element x context) from each source; blind merge and placement to one grain; 143 duplicate sets folded; areas grouped after extraction. Verdicts by #210's covered test, one agent per area, each cited line opened and confirmed.

held_out_new.decision: Once a loading indicator shows, how long must it stay at least, so it does not flicker?

tag.why: Minimum show time is a timing.

held_out_new.decision: Does a menu item that opens further input, or an in-progress label, end with an ellipsis?

tag.why: Platform menu convention (HIG, Windows); label text ending is checkable.

held_out_new.decision: Do controls suppress double-tap zoom (and its tap delay) on touch devices?

tag.why: touch-action: manipulation on controls is the accepted platform answer; no house text.

held_out_new.decision: What colour, if any, is the tap highlight on touch devices?

tag.why: No house text in plugin/skills.

held_out_new.decision: Does the page bounce (rubber-band) at its scroll ends?

tag.why: No house answer in plugin/skills/; matters most in app shells.

held_out_new.decision: Are text selection and hover suppressed on and under an element while it is dragged?

tag.why: Every source accepts user-select none on the drag surface; no house text.

held_out_new.decision: How are keyboard shortcuts shown (platform key symbols) and mapped for non-QWERTY layouts?

tag.why: No house text in plugin/skills.

held_out_new.decision: Does every screen offer a next step or a way to recover (no dead ends)?

tag.why: No house text on dead ends or a next step found in plugin/skills.

tag.why: HTML implicit submission; needs a submit button in the form.

tag.why: Only VG names it; placeholder trailing character is checkable in code.

tag.why: No house text on price decimals found in plugin/skills.

verdict_values.partial: a carried house text answers it; a criterion fails
verdict_values.researched: a docs/research principle answers it; nothing carried does
verdict_values.gap: nothing in the house or impeccable answers it

meta.bound: Paid books are read only where free (Rutter one chapter, Refactoring UI previews, Bringhurst via summaries); Baymard 32 of about 430 articles; MDN single-property reference pages unread; landing pages chosen by title. One coder per source, one merger per bucket, one verdict agent per area, no second coder. The orchestrator chose the sources after reading the notes; the held-out source is the check on that.
meta.stop_rule: #216 Q1 (A): an area is complete enough to fill from when the last two sources add 5% or less and the ledger's sample coverage is 0.75 or more; 90% of Chao2 is reported, not required. Rows still missing come in by the yearly re-scan, founder leads and round faults.

ruling.scope: Q2 (B): every kind of site Manta and MMM Infra have or plan, signed-in tools and dashboards included; shop- and checkout-only rows accepted until such a project starts.
ruling.pace: Q3 (A): fill tiers 0 and 1, then rule again on the pace of tiers 2-4 once #212's planted-fault load test and #224's critic test have measured whether the added rules catch more faults. The order is fixed by jobs[].rank.
ruling.note: Stop numbers were computed before the 13 held-out decisions joined as VG-NEW rows; those rows are excluded from them.

rows.decision: How much padding sits inside a button?
rows.note: No house rule sets padding inside a button.

rows.decision: Is a button's padding adjusted so its content looks optically centred (less on the icon side, trimmed text box)?
rows.context: button with icon or text label
rows.note: No house rule on optical padding or trimmed text boxes.

rows.decision: How round are button corners?

M: https://m3.material.io/styles/shape (tab Corner radius scale, Component changes)

rows.note: Capsule for touch and one standout action, rounded rectangle for dense desktop; no era label; radius-scale and tone principles undisposed.

rows.decision: Do joined buttons in a group use smaller inner corners where they meet?
rows.note: Radius nesting covers shapes inside shapes, not joined buttons in a group.

rows.decision: Does a button's corner radius change when it is pressed or selected?

M: https://m3.material.io/components/buttons (tab Specs, Shape morph; Corner sizes)

rows.note: No house rule changes corner radius on press or selection.

rows.decision: Does a button need a visible boundary (fill or border) to look clickable?
rows.note: A button shows a fill or an edge, 3:1 only where the edge is its one cue, or takes the text rung; vault.affordance checks it.

rows.decision: How much contrast must a button's fill, border or label have against the background?
rows.note: Label 4.5:1 or 3:1 large; labelled button needs no 3:1 edge; icons 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.3, 1.4.11).

rows.decision: What button colour or variant sits on a dark background?
rows.note: On a dark or brand ground buttons take the inverse, light treatment (GOV.UK, USWDS).

rows.decision: How does a button stay visible over a photo, video or busy background?
rows.note: A control on a photo carries its own backdrop, halo or shadow at 3:1 against the image under it (vault.controls-on-photo).

rows.decision: What gives a button its edge in forced-colours (high contrast) mode?
rows.note: A control drawn by a fill or shadow alone keeps a transparent border or outline, which forced colours paints (#283).

tag.why: Forced-colours edge is an edge-role choice that the ruled job holds; notes-coverage answers it.

rows.decision: Is the browser's default button style replaced by the site style?
rows.note: No house rule on replacing the browser's default button style.

rows.decision: Which colour marks action buttons, and do kinds of action take different colours?
rows.note: One reserved action colour, apart from status hues; the danger hue only on a destructive action's final confirmation (vault.destructive-action).

tag.why: Only disposal fails; the danger hue for destructive actions belongs to the ruled job.

rows.decision: How many emphasis levels do buttons have, and how does each look?

R: https://medium.com/refactoring-ui/7-practical-tips-for-cheating-at-design-40c736799886 §7 Not every button needs a background color

rows.note: Emphasis ladder: filled, tonal, outlined, text; carriers dated, review by 2027-10-14.

rows.decision: Which emphasis level does a given action take (alternative, cancel, same-page, component action)?
rows.note: Rung follows task priority, one primary; a destructive action never takes the primary style (vault.destructive-action); left: a rung for each action kind the row names: alternative, cancel, same-page and component actions (#412).

rows.decision: How prominent is the primary call to action relative to the rest of the page?

CX: https://cxl.com/blog/10-principles-of-effective-pricing-pages/ (9. Use a clear call to action.)

rows.note: One main action per view holds the strongest colour; nothing matches or outweighs it.

rows.decision: Does the primary button keep its prominence at every screen width?
rows.note: vault.primary-action checks each view at desktop and phone width.

rows.decision: Which action does the main call to action ask for (sign up, buy, learn more, demo)?
rows.note: S3 takes the main action as the client's goal; no trade-off or era; RA94 not carried, no reason.

rows.decision: Does the main entry call to action get its own button variant?
rows.note: A capsule and one size step up for a standalone key action, as GOV.UK's start button.

tag.why: Larger key-action size is button size by purpose.

rows.decision: How is a destructive button styled?
rows.note: Secondary or text rung beside other actions; filled danger hue only at the final confirmation, the label naming the loss.

rows.decision: Which dialog button is the default (Return key) button?
rows.note: The dialog's default (Return) button is the likely action, never Cancel, and never a destructive one the visitor did not choose (Apple HIG, WAI-ARIA APG); code-checked.

rows.decision: How many primary (high-emphasis) buttons may one view carry?
rows.note: At most one main action per view (Apple HIG, GOV.UK, NN/g); a gate question.

rows.decision: Does an empty state offer an action, and how many?
rows.note: impeccable.md:54 only routes empty states to onboard; manta-element-coverage:193 names the gap.

rows.decision: How many buttons may a view or group show before actions move elsewhere?
rows.note: Only the CTA-count lens: no number, no source, no condition, no era.

rows.decision: How many and which buttons does a dialog or sheet carry?
rows.note: impeccable.md:108 names button labels only; count and set not answered.

tag.why: Button count in a dialog is countable.

rows.decision: Does the primary call to action sit above the fold, or after the explanation?
rows.note: vault.layout puts the CTA on the first screen always; no trade-off against explaining first; founder-kept pages fail it.

rows.decision: Does the call to action repeat further down the page?

UB: https://unbounce.com/landing-page-articles/what-is-a-landing-page/ (What are the key elements of a successful landing page)

rows.note: One semantic colour per status, apart from action; hue per status and theme change unstated.

rows.decision: Which colour does a badge or label chip take?

MS: https://matthewstrom.com/writing/generating-color-palettes/ §So what makes a good color palette?

rows.note: Status chips take semantic colour with text; tint level and static-label colour unstated.

rows.decision: How does a disabled or unavailable element look, and must it meet contrast?
rows.note: Muted but legible, in solid disabled tokens; content shown as unavailable is not disabled (#283).

tag.why: Disabled is one role in the per-role contrast question.

rows.decision: How does the logo stand apart from its background, and must it meet contrast?
rows.note: Grounds follow logo lightness: 3:1 or keyline, else another version; logo link must clear 3:1.

rows.decision: How does an interactive element's colour change on hover, press or activation?

M: https://m3.material.io/foundations/interaction/states (tab State layers, State layer tokens & values)

rows.note: Hover changes tint, elevation or both by project pick; small parts change colour; press goes down.

rows.decision: What colour is a switch's on state?
rows.note: Selected state needs a non-colour cue (house-principles.md:75), but no switch on-state colour.

rows.decision: Which accent colour tints the browser's native checkboxes, radios and sliders?
rows.note: Nothing on accent-color for native checkboxes, radios and sliders.

rows.decision: May a control's background be partly transparent?
rows.note: Glass rule names floating layers and content cards, never a control's own fill.

tag.why: Translucent control fill is a glass question.

rows.decision: What colour does an icon take?
rows.note: Icons reach 3:1 with no condition or era; icon colour itself unstated; stroke rule only.

rows.decision: Does an icon take a gradient fill?
rows.note: No line on gradient fills in icons.

rows.decision: Does an icon use stepped fill to show a level?
rows.note: No line on stepped icon fills for levels.

tag.why: Level indicators (signal, battery, fill) occur in tools and dashboards.

rows.decision: Does a meter or gauge colour encode its value?
rows.note: Nothing on meter or gauge colour encoding a value.

rows.decision: Which and how many colours may navigation labels and icons use?
rows.note: Current page needs a non-colour cue, link colour reserved; nav colour count unstated.

rows.decision: How do carousel and page-indicator controls stay visible over images, and show the current item?
rows.note: Each control on a photo takes its own backdrop or shadow at 3:1; the current dot differs by fill or size, not a faint opacity (Baymard, NN/g) (#316).

rows.decision: Which background colours do the page ground and the surfaces on it take?

R: https://medium.com/refactoring-ui/redesigning-laravel-io-c47ac495dff0 §Changing the site background color; https://www.refactoringui.com/previews/building-your-color-palette §What about greys?

rows.note: Roles, named surface levels and the step between grounds carried (#284).

tag.why: Only failure is disposed; ruled job names the step between grounds.

rows.decision: When may a large area take a strong background colour?
rows.note: Strong colour areas for persuade zones, confirmations and interruptions; working areas neutral (#284). Stays with the whole-page critic: no standard or design system gives a share of a page in strong colour, and 60/30/10 is blog advice from interior design (#410).

tag.why: Only failure is disposed; ruled job names section grounds.

rows.decision: Use a decorative gradient, glow or pattern behind content?

I: skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable -> engine 0.1.11 rule radial-halo; rule radial-spotlight-glow
R: TOC line only; https://www.refactoringui.com/book Full table of contents, Finishing Touches p198

rows.note: A gradient, glow or pattern does one named job, never where visitors work (#284).

rows.decision: In which colour space and hue direction does a gradient interpolate?
rows.note: Oklab, or oklch for far-apart hues, named in the gradient with a plain fallback (#284).

rows.decision: How are colours distributed along a gradient (midpoint, easing)?
rows.note: Colour hints or eased stops place the blend; hard stops only on purpose (#284). Stays with its builder record: no source gives a figure for visible banding or a muddy middle; legacy colours blending in sRGB, CSS Color 4's cause of the grey middle, is vault.gradient-space's line (#410).

rows.decision: Fill heading text with a gradient for emphasis?
rows.note: Emphasis by weight or size; an earned gradient word checked at its weakest stop and in forced colours (#284).

tag.why: Gradient text is one case of when a gradient has a function.

rows.decision: Solid or translucent colour values for fills that sit on varied backgrounds?
rows.note: Translucency only on floating functional layers, solid fallback; never content cards; dated, NN/g 2024.

rows.decision: Opaque or translucent colour for borders and separators?
rows.note: Edges that must reach 3:1 solid; a decorative edge over several grounds alpha (#283).

tag.why: Ruled job names alpha against solid edges.

rows.decision: How opaque or thick is a translucent (glass) surface so its content stays legible?
rows.note: Strong blur, text at contrast floor on worst backdrop, busy backdrops need more blur or solid.

rows.decision: Is saturation or brightness raised behind frosted glass?
rows.note: Nothing in the house, impeccable or docs/research answers this.

rows.decision: How is colour flicker at the top edge of a frosted header hidden?
rows.note: Nothing in the house, impeccable or docs/research answers this.

rows.decision: What colour is a loading skeleton?
rows.note: No house rule on skeleton colour; manta-element-coverage.md:193 records the gap.

rows.decision: How strong (contrast, weight) are dividers and decorative borders, and what colour by default?
rows.context: dividers, separators, card and field borders
rows.note: Dividers and card edges take the weak decorative colour, no 3:1. Thickness is SUR-1.

rows.decision: What colour does the browser toolbar take?
rows.note: Nothing on theme-color for the browser toolbar.

rows.decision: When and how much may the browser toolbar colour change while the page is in use?
rows.note: Nothing on changing theme-color while the page is in use.

rows.decision: Do the browser's own surfaces and form controls follow the page's light or dark scheme?
rows.note: The page tells the browser it has a light or dark theme (the color-scheme setting), so the browser's own scrollbars and form controls match it (MDN, Jul 2026).

tag.why: MDN: declare color-scheme so browser-drawn parts match the theme.

rows.decision: What colours do the scrollbar thumb and track take?
rows.note: Nothing on scrollbar colours.

rows.decision: Do background colours and images print as designed?
rows.note: Nothing on print colour adjustment.

rows.decision: What colours does selected text take?
rows.note: Only impeccable addresses ::selection colours.

rows.decision: Which palette does a colour font use?
rows.note: Nothing on font-palette for colour fonts.

rows.decision: What colours do video captions take?
rows.note: Video captions keep the standard look, white text on a dark box, and viewers can still change caption colours in their player (WebVTT caption standard; US caption rules). A `::cue` rule's text holds 4.5:1 on its own box, drawn over black and over white, and a rule that sets its colour or its box sets both (vault.caption-colours, #410); the viewer's own caption settings stay with the builder (vault.caption-settings).

tag.why: WebVTT and FCC defaults; the viewer can change caption colours.

rows.decision: Declare a background colour whenever text colour is set?
rows.note: Text colour and background colour are always set together, so a visitor's own colour settings never leave dark text on a dark background (WCAG).

tag.why: WCAG F24: set background colour whenever text colour is set.

rows.decision: Is the palette checked for colour-blind viewers?
rows.note: Meaning never rests on colour alone; no step checks the palette under colour-vision simulation.

rows.decision: May saturated red and blue touch?
rows.note: Saturated hues that touch under 3:1 with no white or black between are looked at rendered for shimmer (MDN, Spectrum, brand-palette.md §1.2). Stays with the gate critics: the one figure, Ozolinsh and Muizniece 2015's detection threshold for chromostereopsis, is a lab threshold at equal luminance that would flag almost every red and blue pair, and no source bounds the saturation or hue gap at which an edge shimmers (#410).

rows.decision: How does surrounding colour change how a colour reads (simultaneous contrast)?
rows.note: Each palette colour is judged rendered on its real grounds beside its real neighbours (Chevreul §16, Butterick); a builder target.

rows.decision: Does the palette hold in bright and dim surroundings?
rows.note: Only card borders kept for poor screens; no palette check for glare or dim light.

rows.decision: Does every keyboard-operable element show a visible focus indicator (never removed without a replacement)?
rows.context: keyboard focus on any interactive element, form fields and links included
rows.note: Every focusable part has a visible ring at 3:1; WCAG floors no brand lowers; timeless need.

rows.decision: What form does the focus indicator take: a ring or outline, or a colour change alone?
rows.note: A ring for fields, fill plus non-colour cue for list rows; colour-swap-only named as weak.

rows.decision: With what is the focus ring drawn: CSS outline or box-shadow?
rows.note: Outline, which follows the radius since 2023; any shadow ring backed by a transparent outline (#283).

tag.why: Ring drawing method belongs with the ruled edge-role job; outline against shadow is an edge choice.

rows.decision: How thick or strong is the focus ring?
rows.note: Every ring 2 px or more, an input's drawn outside or as a 2 px border (AAA, relaxable); ring thicker than borders; loud-vs-quiet trade-off stated.

rows.decision: How far from the element, and on which side of its edge, does the focus ring sit?
rows.note: Only inputs get an outside ring; no offset distance; script reach 8 px is an unmeasured guess.

rows.decision: Does the focus ring follow the element's corner radius?
rows.note: No house or research text on the ring following corner radius.

rows.decision: What colour is the focus indicator: a reserved focus colour, the browser default, or one themed from the palette?
rows.note: One focus colour kept for focus alone, two-colour so it shows on every ground (#283).

tag.why: Focus colour against the palette is a per-role contrast choice, which the ruled job holds.

rows.decision: How does the focus indicator keep enough contrast against adjacent colours and on light, dark or coloured backgrounds?
rows.note: Two-colour ring or one ring colour per ground, 3:1 against each ground.

rows.decision: Does one shared focus style serve every component, or does it vary by element type?
rows.note: Style varies by part: ring for fields, fill highlight plus non-colour cue for list rows.

rows.decision: Does the focus ring show on mouse click or only for keyboard navigation (:focus-visible)?
rows.note: Focus styles on :focus-visible, so a mouse press shows no ring (MDN 2026); script owed.

tag.why: The platform :focus-visible heuristic is the accepted answer.

rows.decision: Can a container's overflow or a sticky header, banner or overlay hide the focused element or its ring?
rows.context: overflow hidden containers; sticky headers and overlays
rows.note: scroll-padding under sticky bars; gate fails focus hidden by sticky bar or clipping box.

rows.decision: How do adjacent inputs make room for a neighbour's focus ring?
rows.note: No rule on adjacent inputs leaving room for a neighbour's ring.

rows.decision: Does a non-interactive region that takes programmatic focus (message, skip-link target) show a focus ring?
rows.note: No rule on focus rings for programmatically focused non-interactive regions.

rows.decision: Does a container (card, form group) show focus when a control inside it has focus?
rows.note: No :focus-within rule; the script only counts wrapper pixels as the indicator.

rows.decision: Can keyboard users focus a scrollable region, and does it show focus?
rows.note: A scroller with nothing focusable takes tabindex 0, a role and a name (WCAG 2.1.1, web.dev); script owed.

tag.why: WCAG 2.1.1; axe rule scrollable-region-focusable.

rows.decision: Does keyboard focus show the same reveal or style change that hover shows?
rows.note: Hover-and-focus cue parity stated for prose links only; hover-only research principle not carried, no reason.

rows.decision: May content or controls appear only on hover, or are they shown by default where hover is not possible?
rows.context: touch input; devices that cannot hover
rows.note: Nothing only on hover: what hover shows, focus and tap show too, and a device that cannot hover shows it by default (web.dev, MDN).

rows.decision: Does an interactive element change on hover, and how (fill, cursor, delay)?
rows.note: Hover: tint or elevation by project pick; small parts colour; links non-colour cue. Cursor, delay unstated. Unanswered: the cursor and the delay on hover (#216).

rows.decision: Do non-interactive elements (static tags, bars, dialogs as wholes) show hover or focus styles?
rows.property: hover and focus styles on non-interactive parts
rows.note: Non-actable parts look inert; parts-map lists those with :hover or pointer cursor.

rows.decision: How does an icon button show it is interactive and hovered (background, opacity)?
rows.note: Small parts change colour on hover, never shadow; buttons carry hover and press states.

rows.decision: How does an arrow icon inside a link or button react on hover?
rows.context: arrow icon in a link or button
rows.note: Arrow cue presence is carried, not how the arrow reacts on hover.

rows.decision: Does a card show hover, and by fill change, lift or a movement hint?
rows.note: Card hover changes tint, elevation or both as the project picks; dated, review 2027-10-14.

rows.decision: Does the hover area stay continuous and still when items have gaps or the hovered element moves?
rows.context: grouped items with gaps; hover that moves the element
rows.note: No rule on continuous hover areas across gaps or moving elements.

rows.decision: Does a hover-opened menu or submenu stay open while the pointer travels to it?
rows.note: No house, research or impeccable text answers it.

rows.decision: How long must the pointer rest before a tooltip shows, and does it stay open while pointed at?
rows.note: No house, research or impeccable text answers it.

tag.why: Show delay is a timing.

rows.decision: Does an image scale or rotate on hover?
rows.note: Only impeccable addresses image scale or rotate on hover.

rows.decision: How does a chart respond to hover on a data point (highlight, crosshair readout)?
rows.note: No house, research or impeccable text answers it.

rows.decision: How does text change on hover without shifting layout?
rows.note: Hover and selection change colour, underline, fill or grade, never glyph widths (MDN 2026).

rows.decision: Does hovering one item highlight related items elsewhere on the page?
rows.context: filters and the items they match
rows.note: No rule on hover highlighting related items.

rows.decision: How does hover or press look on an already-selected item?
rows.property: hover and pressed colour on selected
rows.note: No rule on hover or press on an already-selected item.

rows.decision: How does a control show it is being pressed (colour, scale, ripple, timing)?
rows.note: Press goes down (darker, smaller shadow, scaled), never up; ripple struck. Timing unstated. Unanswered: how long a press shows (#216).

rows.decision: Do selected and focused states look different?
rows.note: No rule that selected and focused states must look different.

rows.decision: What marks a selected item (fill, checkmark, underline, highlight)?
rows.context: selectable items, menus, chips, calendar dates, list rows
rows.note: Selected shown by more than colour: check, dot, 3:1 edge or weight; carriers dated 2027-10-14.

rows.decision: Does selection style the whole list row or only its checkbox or radio?
rows.note: No rule on styling the whole row or only its control.

rows.decision: In multi-pane layouts, does the parent list keep the selection highlighted?
rows.note: No rule on keeping the parent list selection in multi-pane layouts.

rows.decision: How much colour do inactive or unselected items carry?
rows.note: Only impeccable addresses colour on inactive items.

rows.decision: Is a button disabled until it can be used (until the form is valid or a choice is made)?
rows.note: No rule on disabling a button until it can be used.

rows.decision: Is a submit button disabled while the request runs, to stop double submission?
rows.note: Only impeccable addresses disabling submit during a request.

rows.decision: Is an unavailable action, option, field or tab disabled, hidden, or kept enabled with an explanation?
rows.context: action or option not currently available
rows.note: No rule on disabling, hiding or explaining unavailable actions.

rows.decision: Are unavailable menu items disabled, dimmed, hidden or kept enabled?
rows.note: No rule on unavailable menu items.

rows.decision: How are unavailable dates in a date picker shown?
rows.note: No rule on unavailable dates in a date picker.

rows.decision: Is a value users must review shown disabled or read-only?
rows.note: No rule on disabled versus read-only for review values.

rows.decision: Do carousel previous and next buttons disable at the ends?
rows.note: No rule on carousel buttons at the ends.

rows.decision: What is the minimum click or tap target size of a control?
rows.context: pointer and touch; icon buttons; dense layouts

M: https://m3.material.io/components/icon-buttons (tab Accessibility, Avoid applying density by default)

rows.note: 24 px or 2.5.8 spacing floor; 44 px if the project sets it. Research calls it partly era-bound.

rows.decision: Is the hit area of a small control larger than its visible shape?
rows.note: House measures the target box, not a hit area larger than the visible shape.

rows.decision: Do targets change size by pointer type (coarse touch vs fine mouse)?
rows.property: size of target by input type
rows.note: Coarse pointer 44 px (WCAG 2.5.5 as the house's touch default), fine pointer the 24 px floor; check-access.py --pointer answers it.

rows.decision: How large and how near to the pointer are frequent targets placed?
rows.note: No rule on size or nearness of frequent targets.

rows.decision: Is the whole composite element (accordion heading, list row, chip, nav item) clickable, or only its label or icon?
rows.context: accordion headers, task rows, menu chips, expanded nav items
rows.note: A composite part with one action is clickable across its whole extent (GOV.UK accordion and task list, NN/g 2015).

rows.decision: How large is the drag area for resizing a sheet?
rows.note: No rule on sheet resize drag area.

rows.decision: Which mouse cursor shows over each kind of region (links, text, resize, drag outcome)?
rows.note: parts-map flags pointer cursor on non-actable parts; no rule says which cursor shows where.

rows.decision: Where does focus go when a modal opens, can it leave while open, and where does it return on close?
rows.context: open and close of a modal dialog or overlay
rows.note: Only impeccable addresses modal focus placement, trap and return.

tag.why: WAI-ARIA APG fixes most of it; a script can open the dialog and test focus.

rows.decision: Where is focus when a menu opens, and how does it move inside?
rows.note: Opening a menu focuses its first item; Escape returns focus to the button (APG); script owed.

tag.why: WAI-ARIA APG menu pattern.

rows.decision: Where does a non-modal popup (callout, floating panel, rich tooltip) sit in focus order; is focus trapped?
rows.note: No rule on non-modal popup focus order.

rows.decision: Does keyboard focus order follow the visual order of the page?
rows.context: keyboard navigation; responsive reordering; side-by-side panes
rows.note: vault.keyboard checks reach only; focus order matching visual order is impeccable only.

tag.why: WCAG 2.4.3; the Tab walk can compare focus order with visual order.

rows.decision: Where does a side component (in-page nav, floating action button) fall in focus order relative to content?
rows.context: side table of contents; primary floating action
rows.note: No rule on side components in focus order.

rows.decision: Does a field or element take focus automatically when a page, form or screen opens?
rows.note: No rule on autofocus at load.

rows.decision: Where does focus land after moving to a new view in an app?
rows.note: No rule on focus after in-app navigation.

rows.decision: Where does keyboard focus go at the end of long-form content?
rows.note: No rule on focus at the end of long-form content.

rows.decision: Where does focus go when a submitted form has errors?
rows.note: After a failed submit, focus moves to an error summary at the top (GOV.UK Error summary).

rows.decision: Does a success banner take focus, and how long does it stay?
rows.note: No line rules on success banner focus or lifetime.

rows.decision: Where does keyboard focus enter a list, and how does it move?
rows.note: A listbox or grid is one Tab stop, entered on the selected item, arrows inside (APG); script owed.

tag.why: WAI-ARIA APG listbox and grid patterns.

rows.decision: How does keyboard focus move through a carousel, and can it reach off-screen items?
rows.note: Rotation stops on focus; slides out of view are inert (APG, MDN inert 2023); script owed.

tag.why: WAI-ARIA APG carousel pattern.

rows.decision: Does focus jump to the next part of a multi-part field when one is full?
rows.note: No rule on auto-advancing multi-part fields.

rows.decision: Can focusing a control change the context (open a page or window)?
rows.note: Focus never changes context (WCAG 3.2.1).

tag.why: WCAG 3.2.1 On Focus.

rows.decision: How clearly does a file upload area show its states (dragging, file added)?
rows.note: No house text, research principle or impeccable source addresses it.

rows.decision: Checkboxes or radio buttons: may the user pick one option or several?
rows.note: Radio buttons for one answer, checkboxes for several (GOV.UK, USWDS, HTML).

tag.why: HTML semantics: radio for one, checkbox for several.

rows.decision: To pick several items, use checkboxes or a multi-select list box?
rows.note: No house text, research principle or impeccable source addresses it.

rows.decision: Show the options inline as radios or put them in a dropdown select, by option count and space?
rows.context: one choice; option count and space

CX: https://cxl.com/blog/form-design-best-practices/ (9. Use radio buttons for small sets of options.)
https://cxl.com/blog/14-steps-to-building-sign-up-forms-that-convert/ (11. Drop-down lists, radio buttons and auto-complete fields)

rows.note: No house text, research principle or impeccable source addresses it.

tag.why: Option-count threshold for radios against a select is countable.

rows.decision: When a list of options is long, let users type to filter it (combo box, search inside the list)?
rows.note: No house text, research principle or impeccable source addresses it.

tag.why: Option count above which a list needs type-to-filter.

rows.decision: Switch or checkbox for an on/off option?
rows.note: No house text, research principle or impeccable source addresses it.

rows.decision: Is an option preselected, and which one?
rows.context: radio groups, menus, payment method, checkboxes
rows.note: No house text, research principle or impeccable source addresses it.

rows.decision: Break a long option list into labelled groups or separator lines?
rows.note: Options judged by grouping and scannability; no condition for when to group, no trade-off, no era label.

tag.why: Option count at which groups start is countable.

rows.decision: How does a radio button show that it is selected?
rows.note: Selected state shown by a dot, check, 3:1 edge or weight, never colour alone; radio stays round.

rows.decision: How can a user undo or clear a radio choice?
rows.note: No house text, research principle or impeccable source addresses it.

rows.decision: Slider or text field for a numeric value, or both together?
rows.note: No house text, research principle or impeccable source addresses it.

rows.decision: Linear or circular slider?
rows.note: No house text, research principle or impeccable source addresses it.

rows.decision: How are the chosen values shown in a multi-select?
rows.note: No house text, research principle or impeccable source addresses it.

rows.decision: How is a date picker presented: compact field with popup, inline calendar, dialog or docked dropdown?
rows.context: date entry by space and screen width
rows.note: No house text, research principle or impeccable source addresses it.

tag.why: Date picker presentation sits with date entry (FRM-107).

rows.decision: Ask the card type with a selector, or detect it from the number?
rows.note: No house text, research principle or impeccable source addresses it.

ruling.why: Arises only on kinds of site no served project has (shops, checkout); reopens when such a project starts (#216 Q2 B, #210 refresh trigger).

rows.decision: Offer a 'same as' checkbox so a matching address is not typed twice?

CX: https://cxl.com/blog/reduce-form-fields/ (Getting more from your lead gen forms)

rows.note: A matching address is offered by a same-as checkbox (WCAG 3.3.7).

rows.decision: Pick a colour or style variant from a dropdown or from visible swatches?
rows.note: No house text, research principle or impeccable source addresses it.

ruling.why: Arises only on kinds of site no served project has (shops, checkout); reopens when such a project starts (#216 Q2 B, #210 refresh trigger).

rows.decision: May dropdown options show icons or images beside their text?
rows.note: No house text, research principle or impeccable source addresses it.

rows.decision: Does a closed dropdown show the full option text or only a compact icon?
rows.note: No house text, research principle or impeccable source addresses it.

rows.decision: May one menu's options change with another menu's choice?
rows.note: No house text, research principle or impeccable source addresses it.

rows.decision: How is each option labelled in a long coded list (code plus full name)?
rows.note: No house text, research principle or impeccable source addresses it.

rows.decision: May a select's default option stand in for its visible label?
rows.note: Only 'visible labels, never placeholders' in a source list; select defaults unnamed; no condition or era.

tag.why: A select with no associated label is detectable in code.

rows.decision: May a select menu serve as site navigation?
rows.note: Function decides: a part that navigates is N and takes link carriers, never another control's look.

rows.decision: Selection dropdown or action menu button?
rows.context: choosing a value vs running a command
rows.note: A command is A (button, verb label); choosing a value is S; the function code decides the control.

rows.decision: Are filter values single-select or multi-select, and is the mode the same across a page?
rows.note: No house, research or impeccable text answers it.

rows.decision: How and where are binary filters (in stock, on sale) shown?
rows.note: No house, research or impeccable text answers it.

rows.decision: Show every option openly, or hide a less-preferred option behind a link?
rows.note: No house text, research principle or impeccable source addresses it.

rows.decision: What does a select-all checkbox show when only some items are checked?
rows.note: A select-all box shows a mixed mark when only some items are ticked (HTML, MDN, Apple).

tag.why: Native indeterminate state; checkable in code.

rows.decision: Which options, including a 'prefer not to say' opt-out, does a sensitive identity question offer?
rows.note: No house text, research principle or impeccable source addresses it.

rows.decision: What controls collect race and ethnicity (checkboxes for several, free text, one or two questions)?
rows.note: No house text, research principle or impeccable source addresses it.

rows.decision: How does a user state language preferences (multi-select, native names, 'other' with text)?
rows.note: No house text, research principle or impeccable source addresses it.

rows.decision: Which contact channels are offered as options?
rows.note: No house text, research principle or impeccable source addresses it.

rows.decision: Offer only subscribe/unsubscribe, or frequency choices, on an email preference page?
rows.note: No house text, research principle or impeccable source addresses it.

rows.decision: How does a user accept terms: a checkbox?
rows.note: No house text, research principle or impeccable source addresses it.

rows.decision: Does a sign-in form offer a 'Remember me' checkbox?
rows.note: No house text, research principle or impeccable source addresses it.

rows.decision: How are required and optional fields marked: asterisk on required, '(optional)' on optional, or both?

CX: https://cxl.com/blog/form-design-best-practices/ (7. Indicate if each field is required or optional)

rows.note: Enquiry forms only: optional fields labelled optional, required marks not colour alone. Asterisk and other forms unaddressed.

tag.why: Required and optional markers are present or not in the label text.

rows.decision: Which fields does a form ask for and require?
rows.context: sign-up, names, postal code, general forms
rows.note: Question protocol: require only what the first reply needs. Enquiry forms only; sign-up, names, postcode unaddressed.

rows.decision: When does a field validate and show its error or valid state: while typing, on leaving the field, or on submit?
rows.note: Never flag a field while it is typed; on a multi-field form flag it on leaving and clear it on the keystroke that fixes it (Baymard), on a one-question page at submit (GOV.UK).

rows.decision: Are a new password's rules checked live as the user types, with a strength meter?
rows.note: No house text, research principle or impeccable source addresses it.

rows.decision: Are form errors shown at each field, in a summary at the top, or both?
rows.note: Status sits beside what it describes; field versus summary not decided; GOV.UK error-summary research not carried, no reason.

rows.decision: Where exactly does a field's inline error sit: above the field, below it, in place of helper text, or in a tooltip?

rows.note: Nothing in the house, impeccable or docs/research answers this.

rows.decision: How is an inline link in running text set apart from the text around it: underline, colour, or both, and with what contrast against the text?

rows.decision: May links in navigation menus, side lists and link-heavy lists drop the underline or the link colour?

rows.decision: What hue do text links take?
rows.note: Link colour reserved, apart from tinted text; hue left to the project, no rule on choosing it.

rows.decision: How much contrast does link text need against its background, light or dark?

R: https://medium.com/refactoring-ui/redesigning-laravel-io-c47ac495dff0 §De-emphasizing secondary content; book ch. 'Accessible doesn't have to mean ugly' p142

rows.note: All text, links included, 4.5:1 or 3:1 when large, against its ground (vault.contrast).

rows.decision: Do visited links look different from unvisited links?
rows.note: Visited colour on article, guide and result lists only, less saturated and still 4.5:1; none on nav, cards, controls (GOV.UK, NN/g).

rows.decision: How does a link change on hover, focus and activation?
rows.note: Hover changes a non-colour property; 3:1 colour links need a cue on hover and focus. Active state unstated. Unanswered: a link's pressed state (#216).

rows.decision: Are underline and link colour reserved for links only, never used for emphasis or on non-clickable text?
rows.note: Link colour and underline reserved for links; headings, labels and emphasis may not borrow them.

rows.decision: How thick is a link underline, and how is it styled?
rows.note: Underline thin; no figure tied to the face's stroke weight; underline form not era-labelled.

rows.decision: How far below the text does a link underline sit?
rows.note: Offset clear of descenders, hover may move it; the era-bound CSS form is not labelled.

tag.why: Only the era label fails.

rows.decision: What colour is a link underline at rest and on hover?
rows.note: Hover changes offset or thickness; no rule on underline colour at rest or hover.

rows.decision: Does an underline break where it would cross descenders?
rows.note: Underlines break around letters that hang below the line (MDN, Typography Handbook).

tag.why: Browser default skip-ink auto; no source asks otherwise.

rows.decision: Which words of a sentence carry the link, and where in the sentence do links go?
rows.note: No general rule on link span; FV item 7 covers email link text only.

rows.decision: How many links does a page or passage carry?
rows.note: No rule on number of links.

rows.decision: Does a link open in a new tab or window, and how is that signalled?
rows.note: No rule on new-tab links or their signal.

rows.decision: How is a link that leaves the site marked?
rows.note: No external-link marker rule.

rows.decision: How is a link to a download or a file (PDF, media) marked?
rows.note: No file-type marker rule; FV item 4 asks an HTML gateway before a PDF, not a marker.

rows.decision: How is a link that needs login marked?
rows.note: No login marker rule.

rows.decision: How large is a link's click area?
rows.context: inline links, navigation links, bulleted link lists
rows.note: Links take the 24 px or spacing floor; links in running text exempt.

rows.decision: Where do reference and related links go in a long page?
rows.note: SEO lens names internal linking only; no placement rule for related links.

rows.decision: Does a page offer a skip link to the main content, and where?
rows.property: presence and position of skip link
rows.note: Only impeccable addresses it; no house text found.

tag.why: WCAG 2.4.1 bounds it; first focusable link to main is checkable.

rows.decision: Is the skip link always visible, or shown only on keyboard focus?
rows.note: Either passes: always visible, or hidden until focus and then shown in full (WCAG G1, 2.4.7, GOV.UK); script owed.

tag.why: WCAG 2.4.7: skip link shows on focus.

rows.decision: How many skip links does a page offer?
rows.context: pages with top or side navigation
rows.note: No house, research or impeccable text answers it.

rows.decision: Do email and phone links show the actual address or number?
rows.note: Email address in full as its own link text; phone labelled 'Telephone:'; small-business and advisor sites.

rows.decision: Are phone numbers shown as tap-to-call links?
rows.note: FV item 7 shows the number; no tap-to-call rule.

rows.decision: How do links appear in print?
rows.note: No print style rule for links.

rows.decision: How does a long word, URL or email address break in a narrow box?
rows.context: long words and URLs in narrow containers
rows.note: vault.reflow bans sideways scroll and cut-off text; no rule on how long words or URLs break.

rows.decision: Is body text hyphenated at line ends?

W: https://book.webtypography.net/Web-Typography_Numerals-and-tables.pdf p.130 §Left-align text, right-align numbers, and align headings with data

rows.note: Ragged body text unhyphenated at a normal measure; `hyphens: auto` with `lang` under 40 characters, or under 50 in a long-word language; vault.hyphens-body (#286).

tag.why: Hyphenation sets the rag, which the ruled job names.

rows.decision: Is justified text hyphenated?
rows.note: Justified text always takes `hyphens: auto` with `lang`; vault.hyphens-body (#286).

rows.decision: How many letters stay on each side of a hyphenation break?
rows.note: Two letters before a break, three after, five-letter words, `hyphenate-limit-chars: 5 2 3`; vault.hyphen-chars (#286).

rows.decision: How many hyphenated lines may come in a row?
rows.note: No more than three hyphenated lines in a row, `hyphenate-limit-lines: 3` where taken, checked on the render; vault.hyphen-lines (#286).

rows.decision: Which character marks a hyphenation break at a line end?
rows.note: The browser picks the hyphen shown at a line break from the text's language (MDN).

tag.why: Browser default hyphen character; no source asks otherwise.

rows.decision: Which language's rules hyphenate a foreign word?
rows.note: vault.lang-parts checks that each lang value is valid; left: a check that each passage in another language carries its own lang (WCAG 3.1.2) (#412).

tag.why: WCAG 3.1.2: mark the language with lang; the browser then hyphenates by it.

rows.decision: Browser automatic hyphenation, or soft hyphens placed by hand?
rows.note: Automatic hyphenation by dictionary; `­` by hand only inside words it breaks wrongly or that overflow on a phone; vault.soft-hyphens (#286). Script owed (#314).

rows.decision: Are headings hyphenated?
rows.note: Headings never auto-hyphenated; vault.heading-hyphens (#286).

rows.decision: How are lines of a multi-line heading broken: balanced to similar lengths?
rows.note:
`text-wrap: balance` on headings, captions and quotations of six lines or fewer, `pretty` in bordered cards, no `
`; vault.text-wrap (#286).

tag.why: Ruled job #208.

rows.decision: How to avoid a lone word on a paragraph's last line?
rows.note: `text-wrap: pretty` on paragraphs and list items, never on `*`; vault.text-wrap (#286).

tag.why: Ruled job #208.

rows.decision: Is overflowing text truncated with an ellipsis or wrapped, and how is the full text reached?
rows.note: vault.reflow bans text cut off at screen edge, not ellipsis truncation; impeccable harden only.

rows.decision: Where in the string does truncation cut: end or middle?
rows.note: No rule on end or middle truncation.

rows.decision: How much text, in lines or words, does a list item carry?
rows.context: list items, previews, list item headings
rows.note: No house, research or impeccable text answers it.

rows.decision: Are a list item's details shown in full or collapsed behind a toggle or 'View more'?
rows.note: No house, research or impeccable text answers it.

rows.decision: May headings, lists and table rows split across printed pages, and are widows and orphans controlled?
rows.note: No print page-break or widow rule.

rows.decision: Does text wrap to a floated element's shape or its box?
rows.context: text beside a floated shaped image
rows.note: No shape-outside rule.

rows.decision: Is body text left-aligned (ragged) or justified?
rows.context: running text, narrow measures, sans and monospaced faces

R: TOC line only; https://www.refactoringui.com/book Full table of contents, Designing Text p111

rows.note: Ragged, never justified, unless the project's rules file names a block.

rows.decision: When may text be centred?
rows.note: Centre only headings, titles, short phrases and passages of three lines or fewer.

tag.why: Ruled job #208.

rows.decision: How many alignments are used in one section or page?
rows.note: One alignment a section or component, a second only where content calls for it.

rows.decision: Is text alignment and side spacing mirrored for right-to-left scripts?
rows.note: In right-to-left languages, alignment and side spacing mirror (W3C Internationalization, web.dev, Apple).

tag.why: Every system mirrors for RTL; logical properties do it.

rows.decision: Is a run of text in another script aligned by its own language or by the interface?
rows.note: No mixed-script alignment rule.

rows.decision: Where does justification put its extra space: between words or letters?
rows.note: Where justification is allowed: hyphens on, space between words, never between letters (#285).

tag.why: House bans justified text, but the choice still stands where the ban lifts.

rows.decision: How are numbers aligned in table columns?

W: https://book.webtypography.net/Web-Typography_Numerals-and-tables.pdf p.130 §Left-align text, right-align numbers, and align headings with data
https://book.webtypography.net/Web-Typography_Numerals-and-tables.pdf p.131 §Align to the decimal point

rows.note: Compared numbers right-aligned in tabular figures at one precision; nominal numbers as text.

tag.why: Ruled job #208.

rows.decision: How is text aligned in table cells?

W: https://book.webtypography.net/Web-Typography_Numerals-and-tables.pdf p.130 §Left-align text, right-align numbers, and align headings with data

rows.note: Table text cells left-aligned, never centred or justified.

rows.decision: Does a column heading take the alignment of its data?

W: https://book.webtypography.net/Web-Typography_Numerals-and-tables.pdf p.130 §Left-align text, right-align numbers, and align headings with data

rows.note: Each column heading takes its data's alignment (Rutter, GOV.UK, MDN; #285).

rows.decision: Are paragraphs separated by vertical space or a first-line indent?
rows.note: Paragraph space or first-line indent, never both (Butterick); no condition for which, no era.

rows.decision: How deep is a first-line paragraph indent?
rows.note: No indent depth rule.

rows.decision: Is the first paragraph after a heading indented?
rows.note: No rule on indent after a heading.

rows.decision: Is a hanging (negative) indent used?
rows.note: No hanging indent rule.

rows.decision: Are lines after a forced line break indented too?
rows.note: No each-line indent rule.

rows.decision: Do quotation marks and line-end punctuation hang outside the text edge?
rows.note: No hanging punctuation rule.

rows.decision: Is line length set by page margins or by paragraph side indents?
rows.note: Measure set by the column; side indents only for set-apart blocks, still in range (#285).

rows.decision: Does a paragraph open with a drop cap?
rows.note: No drop cap rule.

rows.decision: Is the first line of a paragraph styled differently?
rows.note: No first-line styling rule.

rows.decision: How long are paragraphs?
rows.note: FV item 11 limits sentence length, not paragraph length.

rows.decision: Bulleted or numbered list?
rows.note: No rule on bulleted against numbered lists.

rows.note: Bullets are plain geometric markers, icons only when they repeat the item, never emoji (Butterick, USWDS); markup is vault.list-markup's.

rows.decision: How large and what colour is a list marker?
rows.note: No marker size or colour rule.

rows.decision: Which numbering system do ordered list markers use, including nested compound numbers?
rows.note: No counter format rule.

rows.decision: Where does ordered-list numbering start, and does it count up or down?
rows.note: No numbering start or direction rule.

rows.decision: Are headings, sections and footnotes numbered automatically?
rows.note: No automatic numbering rule.

rows.decision: Does a list keep its visible bullets and indent, or is it unstyled?
rows.note: No rule on styled against unstyled lists.

rows.decision: Do list markers hang outside the text edge or sit inside, and how far is the list indented?

LT: https://betterwebtype.com/better-web-typography-for-a-better-web-sample.pdf (ch. 6, Hanging punctuation with other characters, p. 26-28)

rows.note: No marker position or list indent rule.

rows.decision: Is content that looks like a list built with real list markup?
rows.note: Anything that looks like a list is built as a real list (WCAG 1.3.1, Butterick, web.dev); script owed.

tag.why: WCAG 1.3.1: list content uses list markup.

rows.decision: How much space between list items?
rows.note: No list item spacing rule.

rows.decision: How is the gap between an entry and its number at the line's far end filled?
rows.note: No leader fill rule.

rows.decision: How many items does a list or group hold?
rows.context: summary lists, featured lists, process lists, groups
rows.note: impeccable count struck: judge by grouping and scannability; no trade-off, no era.

rows.decision: In what order are items in an option list listed?
rows.note: Filter sets promote important options; no general order rule, no trade-off, no era line.

rows.decision: How are groups within a long list separated?
rows.note: Space where padding separates groups; else divider, full width between sections, inset between items.

rows.decision: List, grid or cards for a collection of items?
rows.note: No house, research or impeccable text answers it.

rows.decision: Key-value list, table or plain list for structured facts?
rows.note: No house, research or impeccable text answers it.

rows.decision: Where do a list row's parts sit: leading visual, label, trailing metadata and actions?
rows.note: No house, research or impeccable text answers it.

rows.note: No subordinate item indent rule.

rows.note: One cue per emphasised run, bold or italic never both, and at most three contrast levels a view (Butterick, NN/g 2021).

rows.decision: How does one item stand out among equal siblings?
rows.context: one item among equals, new content
rows.note: One item among equals stands out by bold, its own fill, size or place, never semibold or a link hue (USWDS, Google Fonts).

rows.decision: How is an important paragraph or a warning set apart in running content?
rows.note: No callout or warning paragraph rule; T carrier covers changing status only.

rows.decision: How is the page's visual hierarchy set and checked?
rows.note: Squint rank against task priority; no condition for clutter or typeface traits (R107, R113 open gaps).

rows.decision: One h1, and heading levels in order without skips?
rows.note: SKILL.md:71 names the heading outline with no rule on one h1 or level order.

rows.decision: How many heading levels?
rows.note: No heading level count rule.

rows.decision: Are heading levels indented further?
rows.note: No heading indent rule.

rows.decision: Sentence case or title case for headings and titles?
rows.note: Sentence case for headings and titles; title case only where a project's rules file names it. The script half is vault.label-case; one case per kind of element across the site, and the page title, stay with the look critic (#314).

tag.why: Ruled job names uppercase against lowercase.

rows.decision: What case do status tags and badges use?
rows.note: Sentence case for tags and status labels (GOV.UK since 2023); Manta's capitals for badges stay its own rule.

tag.why: Ruled job names uppercase and badges.

rows.decision: What case do short UI texts such as list items and tooltips use?
rows.note: Sentence case for list items, menu items and tooltips, one case per kind of element. The script half is vault.label-case; one case per kind of element across the site, and tooltips, stay with the look critic (#314).

rows.decision: How much text may be set in all capitals?
rows.note: Capitals only on a few-word, one-line label, tracked; never a sentence or passage. Script owed (#309).

rows.decision: Are capitals set by style or typed into the text?
rows.note: Capitals used for style are typed normally and set in capitals by the style sheet, so copied text and other languages keep the right case (CSS Text 3); script owed.

tag.why: Set capitals by CSS so screen readers do not spell them.

rows.decision: May a user's name be shown in a normalised case?
rows.note: A name shown in the case its owner typed; no case transform on it.

rows.decision: Straight or curly quotation marks in prose?
rows.note: Curly quotes and apostrophes in all prose, never straight ones (Butterick, Unicode); script owed.

tag.why: Every type source asks curly quotes in prose.

rows.decision: Straight or curly quotes in code samples?
rows.note: Code keeps straight quotes, or it will not run (Butterick); script owed.

tag.why: Code must keep straight quotes to run.

rows.decision: Which way does an apostrophe point?
rows.note: An apostrophe is the curly closing quote, even at a word's start (Butterick, Unicode); script owed.

tag.why: An apostrophe is the right single quote; no choice.

rows.decision: Which glyph for foot, inch, minute and second marks?
rows.note: Foot and inch marks are primes where the face has them, else straight marks, never curly quotes (Unicode, Butterick); script owed.

tag.why: Unicode prime marks; no choice.

rows.decision: Hyphen, en dash or em dash for each use?
rows.note: Hyphen, en dash and em dash each kept to their own job (Butterick, Unicode). The script half is vault.dash-glyphs; whether a pairing or a compound takes its right mark stays with the type critic, as the words' sense decides it (#314).

tag.why: Dash use is fixed by every style guide.

rows.decision: Ellipsis character or three periods?
rows.note: No ellipsis glyph rule.

rows.decision: How are abbreviations marked?
rows.note: No abbreviation marking rule.

rows.decision: How are spelling and grammar errors marked in text?
rows.note: Keep the browser's own spelling underline in fields people write in (MDN).

tag.why: Browser draws the spelling mark in editable fields; keep it.

rows.decision: How is an old price or removed content shown?
rows.note: No strikethrough price theatre: Manta rows; plugin carries only proof never styled as urgency.

ruling.why: Arises only on kinds of site no served project has (shops, checkout); reopens when such a project starts (#216 Q2 B, #210 refresh trigger).

rows.decision: How are editorial annotations marked?
rows.note: No editorial annotation rule.

rows.decision: Are emphasis marks set over each character (East Asian text)?
rows.note: No East Asian emphasis mark rule.

rows.decision: How does text that a link's text fragment points to look when highlighted?
rows.note: No text fragment highlight rule.

rows.decision: How many typefaces does the site use?

LT: https://betterwebtype.com/guide-to-combining-fonts/ (Do you really need more than one font?)

rows.note: One family, or two with fixed jobs, plus a monospace for code alone.

tag.why: Ruled job #208 names how many fonts a site needs.

rows.decision: Which typeface takes which text role (headings, body, interface, code, user content)?

M: https://m3.material.io/styles/typography (tab Type scale & tokens, Customize the typeface)

rows.note: Each face keeps one job across the site, two families at most plus a monospace for code (Butterick, USWDS role tokens).

rows.decision: How to pick a second face that pairs with the first (contrast or harmony, same designer, superfamily, era)?

LT: https://betterwebtype.com/guide-to-combining-fonts/ (Combining fonts from the same foundry / author)

rows.note: No house or impeccable rule on how to pair a second face.

rows.decision: Choose the body face or the heading face first when pairing?
rows.note: No rule on which face to choose first.

rows.decision: Which kind of typeface suits an app or interface surface, against a marketing or editorial one?
rows.note: An app's working surfaces take the interface face, a brand or display face stays on marketing and editorial surfaces (Atlassian, USWDS).

tag.why: Only failure is disposed.

rows.decision: Serif, sans, slab, high-contrast or monospaced face for body text?
rows.note: No rule picks a classification for body text; design-feel maps classes to feel only.

rows.decision: Which typeface fits the text's tone, purpose and the site's goal?

LT: https://betterwebtype.com/how-to-choose-a-font-for-a-project/ (The goal of the website and its content)

rows.note: Display face carries the tone, body face readable first, never a subject association alone; vault.tone-face (#288).

tag.why: Face fit to tone is the ruled tone job.

rows.decision: How good must the chosen face be (professional, free or system; which fonts are poor)?

R: TOC line only; https://www.refactoringui.com/book Full table of contents, Designing Text p94

rows.note: No rule on font quality or which fonts are poor.

rows.decision: Avoid ubiquitous, default or currently fashionable faces?
rows.note: Overused fonts are a level-6 dated ban, review 14 Apr 2027. Rests on impeccable's detector: a ban.

rows.decision: Use the system font stack or a downloaded web font?

LT: https://betterwebtype.com/all-you-need-is-5-fonts/ (How to create your own list of 5 fonts)

rows.note: Only the overused-font ban touches it; no rule weighs the system stack against a web font's cost.

rows.decision: Match the typeface's roundness to the UI's shapes?

M: https://m3.material.io/styles/shape (tab Overview & principles, Use shapes and text in harmony)

rows.note: No rule ties typeface roundness to UI shape.

rows.decision: Where may decorative, script or display faces appear?
rows.note: Display type is brand layer; functional text never takes decoration's look. No size or legibility condition.

rows.decision: How light or how heavy may text be at body and small sizes?
rows.note: Weight 400 or more at body size, black weights only for display; the stroke is measured, not just the weight number (#282).

tag.why: Weight floor depends on stem weight, a face metric.

rows.decision: How many font weights, and which ones, does the site use?
rows.note: Two to four weights, regular and a 600–700 bold, any other given a job; a variable file from three (Atlassian, USWDS, GOV.UK).

rows.note: Optical size is left automatic so a variable font's opsz axis follows the size (#282); left: when to pick a separate static display cut or text cut (#412).

rows.decision: Are confusable letters (I l 1, O 0) distinct in the face?
rows.note: The face tells I, l and 1 apart; codes and data a visitor copies tell O from 0 (web.dev, Atlassian).

rows.decision: How much may letterforms vary within the face (odd letters vs over-uniform)?
rows.note: No rule on how much letterforms may vary.

rows.decision: Is the font's built-in kerning good enough to use?
rows.note: No rule on judging a font's built-in kerning.

rows.decision: Prefer a face with a large x-height for small text?
rows.note: A face with small lowercase letters is allowed, but is set larger to make up for it (#282).

rows.decision: Does the face's set of numeral styles count when picking a body face?

rows.note: A face that will hold compared numbers must have tabular figures, or those numbers move to one that does (Butterick, GOV.UK).

rows.decision: Does the face cover every language the site uses?
rows.note: The chosen face must hold every character the page sets, or the stack names a face for each other script (CSS Fonts 4, web.dev); script owed.

tag.why: Glyph coverage is pass or fail, not taste; a font tool checks it.

rows.decision: Which typeface for code samples?
rows.note: Code and sample text take a monospace face, used for nothing else (Butterick, Atlassian, USWDS).

rows.decision: Where else may a monospaced face appear (identifiers, data), and not merely to look technical?
rows.note: Monospace as a costume is a level-6 dated ban resting on impeccable. Mono for data stays research.

W: https://book.webtypography.net/Web-Typography_Numerals-and-tables.pdf p.132 §Use tabular lining numerals in tables of numbers

rows.note: Tabular figures of the text face for amounts compared down a column; a mono face only where it has none (Butterick, USWDS).

rows.decision: May the logo wordmark use a hard-to-read script face?
rows.note: No rule on script faces in a wordmark.

rows.decision: Which typeface shows mathematical expressions?
rows.note: No rule on a typeface for maths.

rows.decision: Which typeface draws the quotation marks of a quote?
rows.note: No rule on the face of quotation marks.

rows.decision: May list bullets or numbers use another font or size than the item?
rows.note: No rule on the font or size of list markers.

rows.decision: May the font change inside a paragraph?
rows.note: No rule on changing font inside a paragraph.

rows.decision: Do brackets take the bold or italic style of the text they enclose?
rows.note: No bracket style rule.

rows.decision: Let the browser fake bold or italic, or load the true faces?
